title: K Closest Points to Origin
source: canonical K Closest Points to Origin concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of points, where each point is a pair [x, y]. Return the k points closest to the origin (0, 0) by Euclidean distance. Keep the original input order in the output: among points equally close, the one appearing first in the input comes first.

examples.explanation: Distances are sqrt(10) and sqrt(8), so [-2, 2] is closest.
Squared distances are 25, 2, 0, and 8; the two smallest belong to [0, 0] and [1, 1].

hints: Comparing squared distances gives the same order as comparing true distances, and stays in integer arithmetic.
You need the k smallest keys, not a full ordering of all n points.
Sort by squared distance and slice the first k (O(n log n)), or keep a size-k max-bound structure while scanning once (O(n log k)). Either way, a stable selection keeps ties in input order.
solution: Compute the squared distance of each point, select the k smallest with a stable method, and return them in input order: sorting by squared distance and slicing gives O(n log n) time; a size-k heap gives O(n log k). Squaring avoids sqrt and keeps ties exact. O(n) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include ties at equal distance, k = len(points), and negative coordinates

visible.failNote: return the points themselves, in input order
